Victoria was Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1837 to 1901, and from 1876 also Empress of India. Her reign of 63 years, the Victorian era, saw British industry, trade and empire at their height.

She came to the throne at 18, the only child of George III's fourth son. In 1840 she married her German cousin, Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha. They had nine children, who married into royal families across Europe, earning her the name "grandmother of Europe". Albert was her closest adviser and organised the Great Exhibition of 1851, a show of industry in a hall of iron and glass in Hyde Park.

Albert's death in 1861 devastated her. She wore black for the rest of her life and withdrew from public view for years, which made her unpopular for a time.

Her reign saw:

  • The spread of railways, after the Liverpool and Manchester Railway of 1830, and London's growth as the centre of world trade and finance.
  • The Indian Rebellion of 1857, after which the Crown took over rule of India from the East India Company.
  • Gradual reform that widened the vote to many working men.
  • The Great Famine in Ireland and the scramble for Africa.

The monarchy's real power shrank in her time, but she kept firm views and favourites among her prime ministers, Melbourne and Disraeli above all. Her Golden and Diamond Jubilees of 1887 and 1897 became celebrations of empire. Her reign was the longest of any British monarch until Elizabeth II. Her son became Edward VII.
sum: Victoria was Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1837 to 1901, and from 1876 also Empress of India. Her reign of 63 years, the Victorian era, saw British industry, trade and empire at their height.
